title: Sunny and the Autumn Leaves | Bedtime Story
description: Sonny the Quokka walks through a moonlit bush path where fallen leaves have turned every colour at once, and she realises that letting go can be the most beautiful thing a tree ever does. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
The path was covered in leaves.

Not the usual leaf litter of the bush — green and grey and mostly ignored. These were different. Autumn had come through the garden gum trees at the edge of the reserve and left evidence everywhere: gold, orange, amber, dark red. The moonlight caught each one and lit it differently.

Sunny walked slowly, trying to step on every gold one.

Each step made a sound — a soft crunch that felt satisfying and complete. She did it again. And again.

She stopped and crouched down to look at a single leaf.

It was almost translucent. She could see the whole network of veins in it — a tiny map of everything the leaf had been. These were the paths the water had travelled through it. These were the lines that had carried the light in and the sugar out. A whole life's work, visible in the moonlight.

She picked it up gently.

It was dry and light. Almost nothing, now. But it had been something.

She thought: the tree let this go. And it was one of the most beautiful things the tree ever made.

She held it for a moment, then set it back down.

She lay back on the thick, soft carpet of leaves.

They rustled gently under her weight — a small, whispering sound.

The leaf-bed held her perfectly.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, autumn leaves. Goodnight, little one.
